poi_balcon.name: Balcony of Europe
poi_balcon.description: The most famous viewpoint on the Costa del Sol: a palm-lined promenade on a headland jutting into the Mediterranean, with coves below and the Almijara mountains behind.
poi_balcon.short_tip: Go at sunset or early morning, when it's quieter. Next to the Church of El Salvador.

poi_cuevas.name: Nerja Cave
poi_cuevas.description: A gigantic cave discovered in 1959 by five local boys, with vast chambers, columns of stalactites and prehistoric paintings. In summer it hosts a music and dance festival.
poi_cuevas.short_tip: The ticket includes the Nerja Museum. Free visit Monday to Friday at 9:15, booking required, 60 places.

poi_burriana.name: Burriana Beach
poi_burriana.description: Nerja's most popular beach: dark sand, calm water, a promenade full of beach bars and water sports.
poi_burriana.short_tip: Try the paella at Ayo, a beach classic.

iglesia-salvador.name: Church of El Salvador
iglesia-salvador.description: A white 17th-century church next to the Balcony of Europe, with a Mudéjar coffered ceiling and a mural of the Annunciation by Francisco Hernández.
iglesia-salvador.short_tip: Free entry. Right at the entrance to the Balcony of Europe.

ermita-angustias.name: Hermitage of Las Angustias
ermita-angustias.description: A small 18th-century hermitage whose dome is painted in fresco with scenes of the Passion, among the loveliest in the Axarquía.
ermita-angustias.short_tip: Opening hours are short: if it's closed, the whitewashed façade is worth a photo.

museo-nerja.name: Nerja Museum
museo-nerja.description: On Plaza de España, it tells the town's story from prehistory, with the finds from the Nerja Cave in the starring role.
museo-nerja.short_tip: Included in the Nerja Cave ticket; €5 on its own.

verano-azul.name: Verano Azul Park
verano-azul.description: A park devoted to the cult TV series filmed in Nerja, with "La Dorada", Chanquete's boat, as its centrepiece.
verano-azul.short_tip: A must for Spanish visitors. Has a children's play area.

detunda.name: Detunda Botanical Garden
detunda.description: Next to the Nerja Cave, it brings together over 200 species from the mountains of Málaga and Granada, with traditional crops and coastal views.
detunda.short_tip: Free entry. Combine it with the cave visit.

maro.name: Maro
maro.description: A small white village of Nerja on the cliffs, with terraced orchards, the church of Las Maravillas and paths down to quiet coves.
maro.short_tip: From here you can walk down to Maro beach: great for kayaking and snorkelling.

acueducto-aguila.name: Eagle Aqueduct
acueducto-aguila.description: A 19th-century brick aqueduct with four tiers of arches, built to carry water to a sugar mill. You can see it from the Maro road.
acueducto-aguila.short_tip: Viewed from outside; stop at the lay-by on the old road.

acantilados-maro.name: Maro-Cerro Gordo Cliffs
acantilados-maro.description: A nature reserve of cliffs and coves between Nerja and La Herradura, with watchtowers and rich sea beds.
acantilados-maro.short_tip: Best seen from the sea by kayak, or along the paths down to the coves.

frigiliana.name: Frigiliana
frigiliana.description: One of Spain's prettiest villages, 7 km from Nerja: steep lanes of white houses, a Moorish quarter and ceramic panels telling its history.
frigiliana.short_tip: Park at the entrance and walk up through the Moorish quarter. Try the cane honey.
